liability.quote: In determining whether an accusation of academic misconduct is upheld, absence of intention to commit misconduct, extenuating circumstances or ignorance of the rules is not a valid defence.

detection.quote: copy of the plagiarism detection software report (if applicable) and any supporting evidence provided by the AMO (this should also be sent to the student(s)).
the distinction between failure to observe good academic practice and academic misconduct is an academic judgement.

process.quote: Markers of work may raise the issue of poor academic practice with a student when this does not constitute academic misconduct.
The AMO will then refer the case to be heard at the appropriate level.

In judging whether or not there is a case to answer, the AMO may scrutinise all work for a module in which the allegation of misconduct has been raised, even if that work has already been marked and returned to the student.
The student has the right to challenge any evidence presented and to present their own evidence.
The convener will arrange a hearing of the Board
If a student fails to attend without good cause, the Board of Adjudication may choose to proceed in the student’s absence.
A student attending a Board of Adjudication has the right to be accompanied and represented by another member of the University.
Students have a right of appeal against any outcomes
Boards must meet to consider the case within fifteen working days of the convener being appointed, unless there is a compelling reason why this is not possible.
The standard of proof that will normally apply in determining whether an accusation of academic misconduct is upheld is ‘based on the balance of probabilities’.

outcomes.quote: The student must retake the online Training in Good Academic Practice course within five working days of the date of the written warning.
If the student has no prior history of misconduct, a written warning may be appropriate.
Candidate must amend the parts affected by misconduct and resubmit the revised thesis within three months.
Zero for module with a) the right to retake the module for credit only,
if the misconduct is considered egregious, alteration or withdrawal of the degree award.
students who have been found to have committed academic misconduct on two or more occasions must be referred to a University Board.
Sanctions on those found to have committed academic misconduct will, as far as possible, reflect the severity of the offence that has been committed.

definitions.quote: Plagiarism is the act of taking ideas or work from other sources and representing them as if it is the student’s own ideas or work.
Multiple submission is the act of submitting for assessment a piece of work already (or simultaneously) submitted for assessment in the same module, another module or in another context.
Falsification is the fabrication, alteration, or false representation of anything that forms part of a student’s output
Aiding and abetting is any form of assistance with another person’s academic misconduct.
Coercion is where a student puts pressure on another student or member of staff to act in a particular way, or attempts to do so, with the intention of gaining an academic advantage.
